The Harvester is a light IndustrialMech designed for large-scale agricultural operations across the Inner Sphere. Developed by Iroquois Machinery Limited on the Federated Suns world of Shawnee, the original HVR-99 entered full production in 3049 after engineers utilized Star League-era prototype schematics recovered from the Helm Memory Core. Capable of harvesting crops three times faster than conventional machinery, the design spread rapidly across food-producing worlds throughout the Federated Suns within a decade of its introduction.

The Harvester line was expanded significantly in the 3120s when Achernar IndustrialMechs and DiNapoli Industries licensed the design, producing the heavier forty-ton HVR-199 series to compete with newer AgroMechs such as the Demeter. The rugged Harvester chassis has since become one of the most widespread AgroMechs in the former Republic of the Sphere and the Federated Suns alike.

The original HVR-99 mounts a Junkers 120 internal combustion engine that propels the thirty-ton AgroMech to a respectable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour, though the powerplant is notoriously high-maintenance and prone to breakdown if not serviced every thirty work-hours. A fifteen-ton capacity lift hoist occupies the right arm, enabling the Harvester to handle heavy loads and transfer harvested material to trailing cargo trucks, while a combine mounted in place of the left hand actuator allows the machine to cut and gather crops efficiently. A small half-ton cargo bay in the center torso rounds out its carrying capacity.

Protected by LaborHeavy/1 industrial armor, the HVR-99 is better armored than many IndustrialMechs of similar tonnage, a feature originally intended to protect it from large fauna on frontier agricultural worlds. The heavier HVR-199 series expands on this foundation with ten additional tons of mass, a more fuel-efficient engine, and significantly heavier armor capable of withstanding hazardous operating conditions. This robust construction proved fortuitous when operators began stripping the outer armor layer from HVR-199 frames to free sufficient weight for mounting military-grade weapons, creating the various MOD configurations that proliferated across the Dark Age battlefield.

The Harvester owes its existence to the discovery of the Helm Memory Core in 3028. When the New Avalon Institute of Science decoded the cache, a wealth of Star League-era knowledge became available to civilian industry, including prototype schematics for advanced compact IndustrialMechs. Iroquois Machinery Limited, a small firm on Shawnee specializing in harvesting and threshing equipment, seized on these designs to create the HVR-99. The Minette Farming Concern approved the design enthusiastically, and full production began in 3049. Within ten years, the Harvester could be found on almost every agrarian world in the Federated Suns.

The design might have remained a purely civilian workhorse had Achernar IndustrialMechs not licensed and expanded it in the late 3120s. Operating from the world of Achernar, the firm produced the heavier HVR-199 to compete with newer AgroMechs like the Demeter from Wunderland Enterprises. DiNapoli Industries on Ankaa soon followed with its own production line, and by the early 3130s the expanded Harvester had become one of the most common AgroMechs in Prefecture IV of the Republic of the Sphere.

The HPG Blackout of 3132 transformed the Harvester from agricultural tool to instrument of war. As factions scrambled to arm themselves, the HVR-199 chassis proved an ideal candidate for military conversion. Investor Jacob Bannson and Governor Aaron Sandoval fought fiercely for control of the Achernar IndustrialMechs facility, with Sandoval ultimately seizing the plant after the Blackout and using it to produce armed Harvesters for his private forces. Both Bannson's Band of Five and Sandoval's Prince's Men fielded substantial numbers of Harvester MODs, and clashes between these rival formations became a common feature of the fractured political sphere.

During the Liao Insurgency, the Ijori Dè Guāng resistance movement employed Harvesters and other IndustrialMechs against Republic of the Sphere military forces, further cementing the design's reputation as an accessible platform for irregular warfare. A notable engagement in November 3132 saw Harvester MODs from both the Band of Five and Prince's Men clash at a BelOuros scrapyard on Acamar, though analysts found the results inconclusive in determining which MOD configuration held a tactical advantage. The intelligence gathered from security devices at the site, however, proved valuable to Republic Armed Forces investigators.

The Hatchetman was introduced in 3023 as the first completely new BattleMech design produced in the Inner Sphere in over a century. Designed by the enigmatic Dr. B. Banzai of Team Banzai and manufactured by Defiance Industries on Hesperus II, the forty-five-ton medium 'Mech was conceived as a dedicated urban combat platform for the Lyran Commonwealth. The design was notable for several firsts: it was the first production BattleMech to mount a 'Mech-sized hatchet as a melee weapon, and the first to incorporate a full-head ejection system. As a product of collaboration between Lyran and Federated Suns engineers, the Hatchetman also served as a potent symbol of the growing alliance between the two Successor States.

Originally limited to garrison duty in major Lyran cities, the Hatchetman's early combat successes earned it a fearsome reputation as an urban ambush predator. Demand eventually outstripped a single factory's capacity, requiring additional production lines to meet the needs of the growing Federated Commonwealth.

The Hatchetman excels in the close confines of urban terrain, where its combination of ranged firepower and devastating melee capability makes it a formidable ambush predator. Its primary ranged weapon, a Defiance Killer autocannon mounted in the right torso, provides reliable firepower at medium range, fed by twenty rounds organized into two ten-shot magazines, a design feature borrowed from the Federated Suns' Enforcer. Two Defiance B3M medium lasers, one in each arm, supplement the autocannon for close-range engagements, while the Hatchetman's signature three-ton hatchet allows the 'Mech to cleave through enemy armor at point-blank range.

Four Luxor 2/Q jump jets provide a 120-meter jump capability, granting the agility needed to navigate urban environments and set up ambushes despite a pedestrian top speed of only 64 kilometers per hour. The versatile TharHes Ares-8a targeting system is particularly adept at tracking aerospace fighters, providing effective anti-air coverage from the armored sensor globe mounted on the head. The design also incorporates an innovative Full-Head Ejection System that launches the entire head assembly on rocket motors, significantly improving pilot survivability when the 'Mech is in an upright position.

The Hatchetman's primary weakness lies in its light armor protection (only six and a half tons of Durallex Medium plating) and thin leg armor that leaves it dangerously vulnerable in open terrain where faster 'Mechs can exploit its lack of speed.

The Hatchetman's origins trace to the early 3020s, when Dr. B. Banzai of Team Banzai designed the 'Mech in collaboration with the New Avalon Institute of Science. Despite the designer's Federated Suns connections, Defiance Industries on Hesperus II secured the manufacturing contract, and the first Hatchetmen rolled off the production line in 3023. A self-destruct system was fitted to the first thirty production examples but quickly abandoned when it was discovered the mechanism would only trigger under conditions (such as an ammunition explosion) that rendered it redundant.

The Hatchetman received its baptism of fire when elements of Kurita's Fourth Proserpina Hussars raided the Lyran planet of Sevren. A battalion of the Twenty-sixth Lyran Guards, heavily equipped with the new design, lured the attacking forces into a huge industrial park filled with towers, alleys, and dark hiding places. Amidst the complex, the Hatchetmen earned their fearsome reputation, ambushing enemy 'Mechs at point-blank range with autocannon fire or cleaving them apart with their hatchets. The engagement demonstrated the design's devastating effectiveness in urban terrain and cemented its place in Lyran doctrine.

Initially limited to garrisoning large Lyran cities, the Hatchetman's early successes inspired broader deployment. The design soon appeared in Federated Suns units, particularly the Crucis Lancers and First Kathil Uhlans. Following the Fourth Succession War and the creation of the Federated Commonwealth, the Hatchetman was selected as one of the AFFC's standard designs. Demand soon outstripped Defiance Industries' capacity, even after tripling output from Hesperus II, prompting a contract with Johnston Industries to establish a second production line on New Syrtis.

The recovery of lostech in the late 3040s allowed Defiance Industries to create the upgraded HCT-5S in 3049, incorporating an extralight engine, ferro-fibrous armor, and an LB 10-X autocannon. Johnston Industries followed with their own variants after the secession of the Lyran Alliance, including the HCT-5D in 3062 and the fast-moving HCT-6D. The Draconis Combine managed to capture several Hatchetmen following the War of 3039, but Kuritan samurai considered the hatchet a barbaric weapon and the initial program was canceled. Independence Weaponry eventually salvaged the project by replacing the hatchet with a more elegant sword, creating the HCT-5K in 3075.

In the Periphery, mercenaries integrating with the Taurian Defense Forces brought their HCT-3Fs to the Concordat's attention. Protector Thomas Calderon ordered Taurus Territorial Industries to reverse-engineer the design, which they accomplished after much delay by 3054. Production continued until 3066 when the Fighting Urukhai destroyed TTI's facilities. During the Jihad, Johnston's New Syrtis plant was rendered temporarily unusable by Blakist forces, prompting collaboration with Defiance on the HCT-7S, a radical redesign replacing the traditional autocannon with multi-missile launchers developed from Battle Magic mercenary company technology.

The Hatchetman continued to evolve through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era. The Republic of the Sphere fielded its own variant, the HCT-7R, designed at Johnston's relocated Addicks facility under Dr. Bartholomew Banzai II. Defiance Industries responded with the HCT-8S, incorporating Clan-grade technology into the proven platform. During the Free Worlds League's early Jihad campaigns, captured Lyran Hatchetmen were refitted into the HCT-6M, seeing service with the Duchy of Oriente and Principality of Regulus. Throughout its long service history, the Hatchetman has remained a potent urban combat platform, its distinctive silhouette and fearsome hatchet inspiring both respect and dread across the Inner Sphere.

The Hauptmann is the Lyran Alliance's first domestically designed and manufactured OmniMech, introduced in 3060 by Coventry Metal Works. Drawing inspiration from captured Clan Dire Wolf OmniMechs and leveraging experience gained through licensed production of the Draconis Combine-designed Firestarter OmniMech, Coventry's engineers created a ninety-five-ton assault platform intended to serve as a frontline command machine for Lyran Alliance Armed Forces officers. Archon Katrina Steiner named the design to honor the hauptmanns (company-grade commanders who represent the highest-ranking officers to consistently see combat) reinforcing loyalty within the newly restructured LAAF.

Despite having ample room for an extralight engine, the Hauptmann deliberately employs a standard fusion powerplant, a design choice that reduced manufacturing costs while dramatically improving battlefield survivability. With forty-three tons of available pod space and a robust chassis, the Hauptmann provides field commanders with a flexible and durable platform capable of adapting to virtually any tactical scenario.

The Hauptmann's Coventry HAI III chassis mounts a Pitban 285 standard fusion engine, providing a top speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour. While this makes the design one of the slower assault OmniMechs in the Inner Sphere, the standard engine ensures the 'Mech cannot be destroyed by a side torso hit, a critical survivability advantage over designs relying on extralight powerplants. Eighteen and a half tons of Glasgow Limited armor provide excellent protection for a design of its weight class, while CASE fixed in the right torso mitigates the risk of catastrophic ammunition explosions. Eleven fixed double heat sinks provide a solid thermal baseline for all configurations.

The Prime configuration exemplifies the Hauptmann's versatility. Paired ER large lasers deliver effective long-range fire, while an LB 20-X autocannon provides devastating close-range firepower capable of exploiting armor breaches with cluster munitions. Medium pulse lasers, an ER small laser, and Streak SRM-2 launchers complete the close-range arsenal. A Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting and communications, enhancing the survivability of the Hauptmann and nearby friendly units. Six additional double heat sinks allow the Prime to manage its weapons load with reasonable efficiency, though sustained engagement with the full arsenal still generates problematic heat levels.

The Hauptmann emerged in 3060 as the culmination of the Lyran Alliance's drive to develop indigenous OmniMech production capability. Following the Clan Invasion, the Lyran state recognized the critical need for flexible assault platforms to counter Clan OmniMechs on more equal terms. Coventry Metal Works, which had gained valuable experience producing the Draconis Combine-designed Firestarter OmniMech under a technology-sharing arrangement, leveraged data from captured Clan Dire Wolf OmniMechs to create an entirely Lyran design.

Archon Katrina Steiner's decision to name the design after the LAAF's company-level commanders was a calculated political move, reinforcing loyalty within the newly restructured military. The first production models were distributed to hauptmanns serving in the showpiece Bolan, Skye, Donegal, Coventry, and Alarion Jaegers regiments, units that embodied the reformed Lyran Alliance Armed Forces. Additional Hauptmanns reached Skye Rangers formations, while Coventry Metal Works retained several units for factory defense and assigned others to garrison forces on Coventry.

The Hauptmann served throughout the FedCom Civil War, where its durability and flexibility proved valuable in the bitter fighting between Lyran loyalist and Federated Suns-aligned forces. The design's standard engine and heavy armor made it particularly resilient in the attritional campaigns that characterized the conflict. Production continued at the Coventry Metal Works facility through the Civil War era.

The Word of Blake Jihad devastated the Lyran military-industrial complex, and Coventry's factories suffered under the upheaval. Production of the Hauptmann ceased in the wake of the Jihad and Devlin Stone's subsequent military reduction programs. As the Republic of the Sphere era gave way to the renewed conflicts of the Dark Age, Coventry Metal Works explored reviving the design with upgraded Clan-grade double heat sink technology, only to be rebuffed by overstretched domestic Lyran ClanTech manufacturers. Clan Sea Fox's ilKhanate eventually learned of these difficulties through the Chatterweb and brokered a deal under Project Reynard between CMW, Free Worlds League-based Technicron Manufacturing, and Clan Sea Fox to produce the Regent, a ninety-ton purely Clan-technology OmniMech intended as the Hauptmann's spiritual successor.

Despite the Regent's development, the Hauptmann itself remained in service with Lyran units that had maintained their existing machines through decades of conflict. New configurations incorporating mixed Inner Sphere and Clan technology continued to appear during the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, demonstrating the enduring adaptability of Coventry Metal Works' original design.

shared: The Hel is a 65-ton Clan Heavy OmniMech introduced in 3121, developed by Clan Jade Falcon as a successor to the venerable Hellbringer originally designed by Clan Hell's Horses scientists in 2926. Known to the Inner Sphere as the Loki Mk II, the Hel was created in the years preceding Gray Monday to address the aging Hellbringer's longstanding deficiencies in armor protection and equipment capacity. Manufactured jointly by Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten and Csesztreg Industriplex Alpha on Csesztreg, the design has become most common in the Jade Falcon and Hell's Horses toumans, where it serves as a versatile heavy fire platform capable of fulfilling roles ranging from long-range sniping to close-quarters brawling.

The Hel achieves its remarkable forty tons of pod space through a combination of engineering trade-offs that fundamentally distinguish it from its predecessor. A 260-rated XL fusion engine provides a maximum speed of only 64 kilometers per hour, a significant reduction from the Hellbringer's 86 kph top speed that has earned the design the unflattering nickname "Slowki" among Spheroid detractors. This sacrifice in mobility is offset by the installation of a small cockpit and Compound H17 ferro-fibrous armor, which together provide approximately fifty percent more protection than the notoriously thin-skinned original Hellbringer. The T-E H65 Omni chassis utilizes an endo steel internal structure to maximize available tonnage.

The Prime configuration exemplifies the design's long-range philosophy, mounting paired Gauss rifles and ER large lasers in its arms for devastating firepower at extended distances. A torso-mounted Streak SRM-4 provides limited close-range defense when engagement distances collapse. The Multi-Trac targeting system allows MechWarriors to effectively track multiple targets simultaneously, a critical advantage when exploiting the Hel's enormous weapon loadouts. While the small cockpit limits pilot comfort during extended operations, the sheer volume of pod space available ensures that configurations can be tailored to virtually any tactical requirement.

The Hel emerged from Clan Jade Falcon's recognition that the original Hellbringer, despite its iconic status as a Clan Invasion-era heavy OmniMech, suffered from fundamental design limitations that no amount of reconfiguration could overcome. Development began prior to Gray Monday in 3132, with Olivetti Weaponry on Sudeten and Csesztreg Industriplex Alpha collaborating on a design that would retain the Hellbringer's flexibility while dramatically improving survivability. The resulting chassis entered production in 3121 and spread quickly through both the Jade Falcon and Hell's Horses toumans.

The Hel saw significant combat during the Clan invasions of the Republic of the Sphere and Lyran Commonwealth in the 3140s. A notable early deployment occurred on Sargasso in July 3142, when the Ninth Talon Cluster of Clan Jade Falcon deployed a Binary of Hels fitted with B configurations to suppress resistance in the city of Salicastrum on the southern continent of Perusalem. The Long Tom cannons proved devastatingly effective against rebel positions, though a subsequent ambush by a Nova of Wolf-in-Exile forces destroyed half the Binary. The surviving Star regrouped and ultimately forced a Clan Wolf retreat, preventing the world from falling back into Commonwealth hands.

The divergence between Hell's Horses and Jade Falcon tactical philosophies became apparent during Operation Noyan on Biota in 3142, where the Eighty-Second Mechanized Cavalry under Star Colonel Waylon Mehta overran the Falcons' Fifth Mixed Cluster. Both Clans fielded Hels extensively during the engagement, with kinsmen from opposing forces dueling in extended single combat that highlighted the chassis's versatility in different doctrinal approaches.

As combat experience accumulated, the two primary operators developed the Hel along divergent paths. The Hell's Horses focused on leveraging the massive pod space for long-range firepower delivery, producing configurations emphasizing Gauss rifles, missile systems, and energy weapons optimized for standoff engagement. The Jade Falcons, meanwhile, worked to address the "Slowki" reputation by developing configurations incorporating improved jump jets and superchargers to enhance battlefield mobility. This dual development philosophy has produced a diverse stable of configurations that ensure the Hel remains a cornerstone of both toumans well into the ilClan era.

The Helios was developed in the late 3050s by Ceres Metals Industries on behalf of the St. Ives Compact, a small but prosperous state that relied heavily on expensive assault BattleMechs like the Emperor, Pillager, and Victor. Military planners recognized the need for a dedicated bodyguard design capable of keeping pace with its heavier charges while providing meaningful fire support at comparable engagement ranges. The result was a sixty-ton heavy 'Mech purpose-built to complement and protect the Compact's most valuable assets on the battlefield.

The design's straightforward construction and reliance on Compact-sourced components earned it a reputation for ease of maintenance, a quality prized by logisticians across multiple successor states. Though closely associated with the St. Ives Compact and later the Capellan Confederation, the Helios has seen service with ComStar, the Word of Blake, and the Republic of the Sphere over its long production history.

Built almost entirely from St. Ives Compact-sourced components, the Helios offers respectable mobility for a heavy 'Mech. Its Pitban 240 fusion engine drives it to a top speed of just under sixty-five kilometers per hour, while four Swingline X-1200 jump jets provide a hundred and twenty meters of jump capability. This combination allows the Helios to keep pace with the assault 'Mechs it escorts and reposition quickly when threats emerge. Nine tons of Taijian StarShield II armor provides adequate protection for its skirmisher role, though it cannot sustain prolonged engagements against heavier opponents.

The Helios centers its firepower around a MilDouglas "Emperor Bones" series Gauss rifle, giving it the reach to engage targets at the same distances as the assault designs it guards. Two BlazeFire Longshot extended-range medium lasers and a pair of MilDouglas "Duke" SRM-6 launchers round out the armament, providing effective close-range defense against anything that slips past the main battle line.

The Helios emerged from the unique military circumstances of the St. Ives Compact during the Clan Invasion era. When Duchess Candace Liao broke her realm away from the Capellan Confederation in 3029, her military inherited a force heavy on prestigious but costly assault 'Mechs. For years, the Compact supplemented its limited domestic production with purchases from the Federated Commonwealth, but the Clan Invasion in 3049 changed the strategic calculus entirely. As HildCo and StarCorps scrambled to revive Star League-era designs, Ceres Metals engineers worked with St. Ives Military Command officers to create something new: a purpose-built escort and fire support platform tailored to the Compact's doctrine.

The first two production runs were reserved exclusively for the St. Ives Military Command, placing the Helios in every SIMC regiment. Half of the third production run was allocated to ComStar, helping the Com Guards recoup losses sustained against Clan Smoke Jaguar during Operation BULLDOG. Around 3060, trade agreements between Duchess Candace Liao and the Draconis Combine opened the door for new variants incorporating Combine technology. These models were intended both to strengthen the SIMC and to generate export revenue through potential sales to the DCMS.

The reabsorption of the St. Ives Compact by the Capellan Confederation following the Capellan-St. Ives War brought the Helios and its production facilities back under Capellan control. The Capellan Confederation Armed Forces continued to field the design, recognizing its value as a versatile escort platform. During the Jihad, the Word of Blake developed its own variant using captured or salvaged chassis, incorporating advanced technologies like triple strength myomer and improved C3 networking into the proven frame.

The Helios saw renewed interest during the Dark Age, with Ceres Metals introducing an updated model from its St. Ives facility featuring modernized electronics and weapons. The Republic of the Sphere's secretive Republic Institute of Strategic Combat also took interest in the design, producing an experimental variant built on the Blakist-derived chassis for covert operations against Capellan-held worlds. These specialized units, disguised to resemble standard Capellan Helios variants, were used in cross-Wall raids during the late 3130s and 3140s before the fall of the Republic. The ultimate fate of the surviving RISC Helios units remains unknown.

The Hermes III designation originally applied to the Draconis Combine's HER-4K variant of the Hermes II, but Luthien Armor Works' extensive post-Jihad upgrades have effectively created a new chassis bearing the same name. Built from salvaged HER-4K frames recovered from militias and scrapyards across the Combine, these modernized 'Mechs incorporate advanced technology that transforms the aging scouts into capable contemporary reconnaissance platforms.

Luthien Armor Works' involvement reflects the DCMS's urgent need to reconstitute its reconnaissance forces following the devastating losses of the Jihad. Rather than waiting for new construction, LAW's engineers developed comprehensive refit packages that could rapidly return damaged Hermes III frames to frontline service while dramatically improving their combat capabilities.

The upgraded Hermes III retains the original's role as a heavy scout and skirmisher while significantly enhancing its combat potential. The refitted snub-nose PPCs provide effective firepower within 270 meters, offering pilots a measure of parity against contemporary medium 'Mechs without the range disadvantages of the original's large lasers. The sacrifice of the traditional flamer for an additional hand actuator improves the 'Mech's ability to manipulate objects during extended operations, a practical consideration for reconnaissance units operating far from supply lines.

Advanced electronics distinguish the modernized Hermes III from its predecessor. The proven Irian E.A.R. communications system receives upgrades including Guardian ECM integration and C3 slave capability, allowing the 'Mech to coordinate with Combine tactical networks while providing electronic countermeasures protection. The Cat's Eyes targeting computer enhances accuracy, partially compensating for the snub-nose PPCs' reduced effective range compared to standard particle cannons.

The chassis itself receives attention, with an Irian-Ost-LAW hybrid frame incorporating improvements developed through the partnership between the original manufacturer and its Combine counterpart. A GM 240 XL engine maintains the design's mobility while Samarkand Royal Heavy ferro-fibrous armor provides improved protection without excessive weight penalties.

The original Hermes III emerged during the First Succession War when Ostmann Industries' Kuritan branch recognized the potential in Hermes II chassis imported under the Concord of Kapteyn. Their engineers transformed these Free Worlds League scouts into energy-focused strikers that eliminated ammunition dependency, creating a variant that proved popular enough to receive its own designation despite being built on the same forty-ton frame.

The Jihad's devastation of DCMS reconnaissance forces created urgent demand for capable scout platforms. Rather than waiting for new construction to fill the gap, Luthien Armor Works recovered damaged and abandoned HER-4K frames from across the Combine, developing comprehensive upgrade packages that could rapidly return these veterans to service. The New Samarkand Refit Facility became the primary center for this work, processing salvaged chassis and upgrading them to contemporary standards.

The upgraded Hermes III received its first combat test on Mualang in 3084 during a Ghost Bear incursion. Elements of the First Sword of Light's Third Battalion deployed several HER-6Ks on a flanking maneuver that surprised the Ninth Provisional Garrison Cluster, demonstrating the modernized design's reconnaissance and fire support capabilities. The engagement marked the end of serious Ghost Bear offensive operations on the world.

Subsequent deployments during the Second Combine-Dominion War further validated the design. At Trondheim in 3100, Hermes IIIs from the Eleventh Ghost were among the first 'Mechs to reach the ground during heavily contested combat drops, using their C3 integration to direct fire support while still descending. Luthien Armor Works continues developing new variants, with the HER-7K representing their latest effort to create the definitive version of this venerable chassis.

text.overview:
The Hammerhands was introduced in 2475 by Achernar BattleMechs as the Federated Suns' second exclusive BattleMech design. After a decade of reviewing complaints about the BattleAxe, Achernar's engineers increased the chassis weight to seventy-five tons while de-rating the engine, replacing the earlier design's troublesome particle projection cannons with a pair of heavy autocannons mounted in each arm. The modifications were extensive enough that Achernar chose to rebrand the design entirely, christening it the Hammerhands in honor of the devastating firepower loaded in each arm.

The Hammerhands quickly became the Federated Suns' signature military machine, enjoying considerable popularity within the AFFS for decades. Though later eclipsed by more advanced designs, the Hammerhands earned an enduring place in Davion military tradition as the machine that cemented the Federated Suns' longstanding preference for autocannon-armed BattleMechs.
text.capabilities:
The Hammerhands design philosophy centered on solving the BattleAxe's chronic overheating by replacing its particle projection cannons with a pair of Mydron Model B Autocannon/10s, one mounted in each arm. This traded energy weapon dependency for ammunition-based reliability, giving MechWarriors sustained firepower without crippling heat buildup. Backed by ChisComp 38 medium lasers in each arm and a shoulder-mounted Harpoon-6 SRM-6 rack, the weapons platform delivers punishing volleys at both medium and close range.

The seventy-five-ton chassis carries StarGuard III armor in respectable quantities, though protection remains secondary to firepower in the design's priorities. Rawlings 50 jump jets provide ninety meters of jump capability, an unusual feature for a heavy 'Mech of the Age of War era that many Federated Suns pilots were slow to embrace. Ground speed suffers at only fifty-four kilometers per hour, making the Hammerhands among the slower designs in its weight class.

The autocannon-heavy loadout created a favorable damage-to-heat ratio that endeared it to generations of Davion MechWarriors and sparked the Federated Suns' enduring fascination with ballistic weaponry. The barrel-shrouded arm mounts also allow effective physical combat without compromising the primary weapons.
text.deployment: This specialized variant was fielded by the AFFS Prince's Champion on Royal during the Second Hidden War, the covert conflict between the Federated Suns and the Draconis Combine waged beneath the Star League's notice. The modification replaces the standard autocannons with a pair of LB 10-X autocannons capable of firing both solid shot and cluster rounds for increased versatility. The jump jets are removed to free tonnage for three additional heat sinks and two extra tons of armor, creating a more durable platform suited to sustained engagements.
text.battleHistory:
The Hammerhands emerged from Achernar BattleMechs in 2475 as a direct response to the failures of the BattleAxe, the Federated Suns' first exclusive BattleMech design. Where the BattleAxe had been plagued by chronic overheating from its particle projection cannons, the Hammerhands traded those weapons for Mydron Model B autocannons, a change that proved enormously popular with Davion MechWarriors. The design quickly became the chosen BattleMech of the Federated Suns military, spreading through the AFFS so rapidly that the Terran Hegemony took notice.

The Hegemony ultimately drew on both the Hammerhands and the BattleAxe as inspiration when StarCorps Industries created the Warhammer in 2515. Achernar fiercely protested this appropriation of their flagship designs, but the Warhammer proved superior in virtually every measurable respect. Improved secondary weapons, better heat management, and higher ground speed combined to render the Hammerhands obsolete. In repeated confrontations between the two designs, the Warhammer prevailed decisively, and the Hammerhands earned the derisive nickname the "poor man's Warhammer." Both the Hammerhands and BattleAxe gradually faded from frontline service.

Even as the design disappeared from active inventories, the autocannons it had championed endured. The Mydron Corporation's prominence, built on the Hammerhands' success, helped establish the autocannon as the Federated Suns' weapon of choice. Military media highlighted the weapons' favorable damage-to-heat ratio, and a generation of cadets grew up seeking autocannon-equipped 'Mechs, cementing a doctrinal preference that would persist for centuries. Mydron would eventually locate many of its factories in the Hegemony, only to have them destroyed in the Amaris Coup.

The Hammerhands' revival came during the Jihad, when the Federated Suns military-industrial complex resurrected several Age of War designs. Achernar BattleMechs on New Avalon and Hessen IndustrialWorks on New Hessen both restarted production lines, initially fielding updated versions of the venerable design for the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns. The modernized variants incorporated advanced technologies including C3 networking, rotary autocannons, and triple-strength myomer, transforming the ancient chassis into a credible Jihad-era combatant. Production of the HMH-6D and HMH-6E continued well beyond the Jihad, with Achernar maintaining active lines into the ilClan era.

text.deployment: Introduced in the late 3120s by Achernar IndustrialMechs, the HVR-199 is a substantial expansion of the original Harvester concept. Weighing forty tons, the design mounts a more fuel-efficient engine and significantly heavier armor than its predecessor, enabling operations in hazardous environments where lighter AgroMechs would be at risk. Two tons of cargo space and robust industrial equipment made it competitive with contemporary designs like the Demeter. DiNapoli Industries on Ankaa produces the design under license, and between the two manufacturers, the HVR-199 became one of the most widespread AgroMechs in the former Republic of the Sphere.

text.deployment: A further field modification built on the HVR-199M platform, the 199M-M replaces the cargo bay with four vehicular mine dispensers. This conversion transforms the Harvester from a direct-fire combatant into an area denial platform, capable of seeding minefields to slow or channel enemy movement. The modification has been spotted in use among various irregular forces, leveraging the Harvester's agricultural origins to deploy mines across wide areas with a machine originally designed to work open fields.

text.overview: Born from the Draconis Combine’s desperate need to convert technological windfalls into lasting military advantage, the Hatamoto-Chi is one of the most successful BattleMech redesigns in Inner Sphere history. When Kanrei Theodore Kurita received ComStar’s gift of Star League-era BattleMechs prior to the War of 3039, he ordered Luthien Armor Works to reverse-engineer the advanced Thug and adapt its weaponry to the existing Charger production line. Rather than building an entirely new chassis from scratch, LAW engineers grafted the Thug’s devastating twin-PPC armament and SRM racks onto the Charger’s robust frame, cutting manufacturing time in half and greatly accelerating the DCMS’s reconstruction after the Fourth Succession War. The resulting eighty-ton assault ’Mech became a symbol of the Dragon’s resurgence, and the Charger chassis’s spacious torso cavities and easily reconfigurable arm assemblies spawned an entire family of variants, from the standard Hatamoto-Chi to the specialized Hatamoto-Hi, Kaze, Ku, Mizo, Suna, Godai, and the amphibious Hatamoto-Kaeru.
text.capabilities:
Despite being a crude duplication of a design produced centuries earlier, the Hatamoto-Chi’s pair of particle projection cannons backed by torso-mounted SRM-6 racks makes it a lethal combatant at any range. The Mitchell Argon armor surrounding the Earthwerks VOL chassis provides excellent protection, and the design’s modular construction (inherited from the Charger) makes battlefield repairs remarkably straightforward. Technicians regularly rebuilt destroyed Hatamoto-Chi to full combat capability within days, a feat that repeatedly confounded opposing intelligence services who could not determine whether they were facing new production or rebuilt machines.

The principal weakness of the original HTM-26T was its limited heat dissipation. Only seventeen heat sinks cooled the design, leaving a Hatamoto-Chi running dangerously warm when firing both PPCs on the move, a consequence of retaining the Charger’s conventional chassis rather than the Thug’s original endo steel frame. The HTM-27T production model addressed this deficiency once the Combine could mass-produce endo steel, freeing weight for additional ammunition and CASE protection. Later variants incorporated double heat sinks, extended-range weaponry, C3 networking, and even underwater maneuvering units, demonstrating the chassis’s extraordinary adaptability.
text.deployment: A factory refit of the Hatamoto-Kaze produced by Maltex Corporation on Unity, this variant adds a conventional C3 slave to the mix and replaces the older missile systems with multi-missile launchers. Less elaborate than other Hatamoto factory refits, the modification nonetheless keeps the Kaze variant current with modern networking and weapons technology.
text.battleHistory:
The Hatamoto-Chi’s origins trace to the political maneuvering of the future Coordinator Theodore Kurita. When ComStar provided the Combine with hundreds of SLDF BattleMechs, Theodore looked beyond the immediate military advantage to the long-term technological potential. Several Thugs (“accidentally” left with Star League technology by negligent ComStar technicians) were secretly shipped to Luthien Armor Works for reverse engineering. LAW engineers elected to base the new design on their existing Charger line, and to throw MIIO off the trail, the design was released under the cover of a fictitious “Maltex Corporation,” leading to an erroneous listing of the primary factory as Errai.

Prototype HTM-26Ts were field-tested during the War of 3039, where their appearance confused Allied battle computers that mistook them for standard Chargers. Post-war feedback sessions between MechWarriors and LAW observers produced heated exchanges over the design’s limited SRM ammunition, the pilots complained of running dry in combat, while engineers noted that the empty ammunition bays had actually prevented several machines from being destroyed by internal explosions. The debate ended with the HTM-27T, which incorporated endo steel construction, additional ammunition, and CASE protection.

Production expanded rapidly through the 3040s. LAW sold the design and the expensive Al Na’ir endo steel facility to Yori ’Mech Works, using the proceeds to upgrade their own production lines. Independence Weaponry on Quentin added a second production source, and the Hatamoto-Chi became one of the standard low-end assault ’Mechs of the DCMS, with nearly every battalion containing at least one variant. The HTM-28T from Independence Weaponry’s Quentin lines represented a complete redesign with jump jets, double heat sinks, and extended-range PPCs.

Maltex Corporation (which had started as a cover identity) eventually became a real manufacturer on Unity, producing the Hatamoto-Suna with innovative ballistic-reinforced armor, the electronics-heavy Hatamoto-Godai command variant, and the amphibious Hatamoto-Kaeru. The Hatamoto series has remained one of the DCMS’s most iconic BattleMech families through the ilClan era, with Maltex’s HTM-30T incorporating heavy PPCs and the latest armor technology.

text.deployment: This variant represents Dr. Banzai's original prototype configuration for the Hatchetman. The design incorporated heat sinks directly into the hatchet blade, intending the melee weapon to serve double duty as a heat dissipation surface. However, the structural reinforcement required to make the hatchet combat-effective consumed more mass than anticipated, forcing a reduction from fourteen heat sinks to eleven. This configuration was ultimately refined into the production HCT-3F, with the hatchet-mounted heat sink concept abandoned in favor of a more practical weapon design.

Dr. Banzai's second attempt to integrate heat sinks into the Hatchetman's hatchet, this variant sacrificed top speed to assault-class levels in order to maintain the original complement of fourteen heat sinks alongside the hatchet-mounted cooling concept. A handful of examples were produced before a contentious evaluation conference on Furillo resulted in the variant's cancellation. The dramatic reduction in mobility was deemed unacceptable for a medium 'Mech intended for urban combat, where speed and agility are essential for effective ambush tactics.

Born from the desperation of the Capellan Confederation's Operation Celestial Reward, this variant was assembled from whatever components Johnston Industries had available as parts and consumables ran critically low on New Syrtis. A battery of extended-range small and medium lasers provides backup firepower to a capacitor-enhanced snub-nose PPC, while triple-strength myomer transforms the variant into a devastating melee combatant when running hot. A Guardian ECM suite provides electronic protection, and heavier armor than the standard 5D improves survivability. The 5DT proved instrumental in bolstering the defenders of New Syrtis when Capellan forces invaded in 3145.

Another Johnston Industries product, this variant takes the unprecedented step of removing the Hatchetman's jump jets entirely, dedicating the saved tonnage to armored components protecting the fusion engine and a compact gyro. Armed with four extended-range medium lasers split between the left arm and right torso, the 7D also mounts a Guardian ECM suite for electronic protection. Nine tons of standard armor provide solid protection for a design that prioritizes resilience and survivability over the mobility traditionally associated with the Hatchetman line, representing a significant philosophical departure from earlier variants.

text.overview: Compared to Johnston Industries’ radical Hatchetman HCT-7D and the Republic’s experimental HCT-7R, Defiance’s HCT-8S takes a more measured approach by combining—and improving upon—features of the -6S and -7S models. While the ’Mech’s primary firepower is still supplied by a trusty Defiance Disintegrator LB 10-X autocannon, it is now backed-up by a pair of Clan-grade ER medium lasers. Its speed is enhanced by a ClanTech engine as used on most of Defiance’s current products, also improving survivability. Double-strength heat sinks round out the package, allowing the -8S to operate without fear of heat build-up.
text.notableUnits: First Leutnant Cory Inglis: A new member of the Fifth Lyran Regulars in 3144, the then-sergeant’s trial by fire came the following year in the form of a determined assault by elements of the Jade Falcon’s Gamma Galaxy. Assigned to the factory world of Loxley along with six of the Regulars’ twelve companies, the week-long battle saw four of those companies destroyed. In the midst of the action, his heavily damaged unit was twice combined with other battered companies, and Inglis was breveted to leutnant as casualties mounted.:br::br::tab:Fighting a guerilla defense amongst the Gray Mountains, he personally claimed three OmniMech kills in as many days, all of which were heavier units. His actions went a long way to safeguard Loxley’s vital factories and earned him a full commission to first leutnant, while the Fifth Regulars as a whole were awarded the Falconslayers Medallion for their efforts. Playing an active role in rebuilding the unit, intelligence reports suggest Inglis may soon be promoted to hauptmann.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration A shifts the Hauptmann to a close-combat role, mounting four ER medium lasers and paired SRM-6 launchers linked to an Artemis IV fire control system for devastating short-range engagements. A Gauss rifle provides a reliable long-range striking capability for closing with an enemy. Three jump jets grant ninety meters of jumping distance (remarkable mobility for a ninety-five-ton machine) allowing pilots to exploit terrain and outmaneuver heavier opponents. The ER medium lasers were especially sourced from Free Worlds League manufacturers, reflecting the cross-border trade that characterized the pre-Civil War era. Six additional double heat sinks manage the configuration's heat load effectively.

Alternate Configuration B adopts a multi-range combat philosophy, mounting paired ER PPCs for punishing long-range fire and three medium pulse lasers for close defense. The centerpiece of this configuration is an Ultra Autocannon/20, capable of delivering massive damage at close range with its double-fire capability. However, the configuration sacrifices heat management for raw firepower, carrying only five additional double heat sinks, insufficient for sustained use of the full arsenal. Pilots must exercise strict fire discipline to avoid dangerous heat buildup, particularly when combining the ER PPCs with the autocannon.

Developed during the Jihad, Alternate Configuration D transforms the Hauptmann into a dedicated command unit. A C3 master computer and targeting computer are mounted in the left torso, enabling the 'Mech to coordinate networked lancemates while enhancing its own weapons accuracy. A Heavy PPC and Gauss rifle provide potent long-range firepower, supplemented by paired Rocket Launcher 10 racks in each arm for devastating alpha strikes against targets of opportunity. Two ER medium lasers round out the arsenal for close engagements, making this configuration a capable battlefield coordinator that does not sacrifice offensive punch for its command role.

Also developed during the Jihad, Alternate Configuration E emphasizes ranged versatility. A Gauss rifle in the right arm delivers precise long-range kinetic impacts, while a plasma rifle in the left arm provides both direct damage and the ability to induce dangerous heat buildup in enemy 'Mechs. Both arms sacrifice lower arm actuators to permit arm-flipping, expanding the configuration's firing arcs significantly. Paired MML-5 launchers in the side torsos provide flexible missile support, capable of switching between long-range and short-range munitions as the tactical situation demands. Three tons of CASE-protected ammunition sustain the missile systems through extended engagements.

Appearing during the Dark Age, this configuration mounts an Improved Heavy Gauss Rifle as its primary weapon, delivering devastating kinetic energy at significant range with improved ammunition efficiency over the standard model. A Heavy PPC in the right arm provides complementary long-range energy fire, while three Medium X-Pulse lasers handle close-range defense with enhanced accuracy. An Angel ECM suite offers superior electronic warfare capability beyond the standard Guardian system used in earlier configurations, and CASE II protects the ammunition supply with improved containment technology that preserves more of the 'Mech's internal structure in the event of an explosion.

This mixed-technology configuration leverages Clan-specification weapons to extend the Hauptmann's effective engagement range. A Clan ER PPC serves as the primary weapon, delivering superior range and damage compared to Inner Sphere equivalents. Three LRM-15 launchers distributed across both arms and the right torso provide overwhelming indirect fire capability, making this configuration particularly effective in a fire support role. A C3 boosted master computer enables network coordination with enhanced resistance to electronic countermeasures, making the M configuration an ideal command platform for combined-arms operations during the Dark Age conflicts.

This mixed-technology configuration represents one of the most destructive Hauptmann loadouts, mounting dual Clan-specification Ultra AC/20s in the side torsos. Each autocannon carries three tons of ammunition, providing sustained close-range firepower capable of overwhelming virtually any opponent. Paired TSEMP Cannons in the arms deliver electromagnetic disruption capability, able to shut down enemy electronics and 'Mech systems with concentrated fire. An ER small laser in the head provides minimal backup weaponry. The left torso is protected by CASE II while the right torso carries standard CASE, reflecting the asymmetric internal layout. This configuration excels in close-range engagements where its combined ballistic and electromagnetic arsenal can rapidly disable and destroy targets.

text.overview: The Havoc is a thirty-five-ton light BattleMech designed by Adam Tech Industries and manufactured at their facility on Abadan in the former Free Worlds League. Entering production around 3112, the design was inspired by the venerable JR7-K Jenner and aimed to improve upon many of that proven striker's shortcomings. Adam Tech, a start-up firm that converted a small industrial component manufacturing center into full 'Mech production, marketed the Havoc exclusively to light BattleMech pilots with the slogan "In any battle, you only pilot one 'Mech." This tagline earned the design its widely recognized nickname, "the One." The Havoc proved an immediate commercial success on the Dark Age market, appealing to MechWarriors who demanded quality and survivability from their light chassis.
text.capabilities:
Built on an X-H54 Endo Steel frame and powered by a Hermes 280 XL engine, the Havoc achieves a top speed of one hundred twenty-nine kilometers per hour, placing it among the fastest designs in its weight class. Five Chilton 360 jump jets provide a leap distance of one hundred fifty meters, granting excellent repositioning capability in broken terrain. Jolassa 328 Ferro-Fibrous armor with CASE II protection delivers a level of survivability rarely seen on a light 'Mech, approaching the protection of many medium-weight designs and allowing the Havoc to absorb punishment that would cripple most of its peers.

The primary armament consists of four Diverse Optics Extended-Range Medium Lasers paired with a Hovertec Quad SRM-4 launcher fed by two tons of ammunition, enabling specialty munitions loadouts as the tactical situation demands. The heart of the design is its Octagon Tartrac System E targeting and tracking suite, widely considered the finest short-range fire control package available at the time of introduction. The Tartrac carries over three thousand target profiles in its stock database and is field-upgradable. In trials, the Octagon distinguished between similar target silhouettes faster than any competing system tested, drawing favorable comparisons to the Garret D2j. This exceptional fire control allows the Havoc to maximize weapons accuracy during high-speed engagements, though aggressive pilots may find the heat burden challenging when firing all weapons simultaneously.
text.deployment: A dedicated reconnaissance variant, this variant retains the four Diverse Optics Extended-Range Medium Lasers of the base model but replaces the SRM-4 launcher with a pair of One-Shot SRM-2 racks for emergency close defense. The freed tonnage accommodates a Bloodhound Active Probe for enhanced electronic detection and a Targeting Computer to improve weapons accuracy. The removal of CASE II and one double heat sink, combined with a switch from standard Ferro-Fibrous to Light Ferro-Fibrous armor plate, creates enough weight savings to mount three additional jump jets, extending the Havoc's leap capability to two hundred forty meters. This significantly enhanced mobility and advanced sensor suite transform the design into an exceptionally capable scout platform that can locate and designate targets for heavier lancemates while remaining extremely difficult to pin down.
text.battleHistory:
Adam Tech Industries established itself on Abadan by purchasing and expanding a small industrial component manufacturing center into a full BattleMech production facility. The Havoc was the company's first design, entering production during the early years of the thirty-second century when the Republic of the Sphere still held sovereignty over Abadan. Unlike many Dark Age manufacturers that cut corners to rush products to an equipment-starved market, Adam Tech prioritized build quality and component reliability, selecting widely available materials and proven subsystems that ensured ease of maintenance and broad parts availability.

As political boundaries shifted during the tumultuous Dark Age, Abadan's sovereignty changed hands multiple times. The Republic of the Sphere's contraction saw the world briefly classified as independent before the reformed Free Worlds League reasserted control. Through each transition, Adam Tech maintained production, and the Havoc found its way into the hands of multiple factions operating in the former League territories.

The Marik-Stewart Commonwealth deployed Havocs in the defense of Concord during skirmishes with the Lyran Commonwealth in early 3135. In one notable engagement, a pair of Havocs squared off against a Wolfhound and two Mjolnirs in the densely forested Western Wilderness region. During fifteen minutes of heated combat, the Havocs disabled both Mjolnirs and sent the Wolfhound running, demonstrating the design's potency against heavier opposition. When one Havoc took a hit to its ammunition magazine, the CASE II system prevented the destruction of the 'Mech while keeping it combat-ready, validating Adam Tech's emphasis on pilot survivability.

The Havoc also participated in an unlikely engagement on Lyons alongside mercenary forces from Zelandia Unbound, where the design's exceptional speed proved decisive in a running pursuit against heavier 'Mechs. The Havoc's ability to execute high-speed attack runs and use its jump jets to evade return fire from even assault-weight opponents cemented its reputation as a premier light striker. Production has continued on Abadan into the ilClan era under restored Free Worlds League governance, with Adam Tech expanding its product line to include the GBT-1G Gambit as a complementary long-range design.

text.deployment: Alternate Configuration F emulates the eighty-five-ton Hellstar by mounting four ER PPCs, delivering withering long-range energy firepower from a significantly lighter and cheaper platform. The remaining pod space is dedicated entirely to thermal management, with ten additional double heat sinks and six coolant pods working to maximize the weapons' sustainable fire rate. This single-minded focus on energy weapon output and cooling creates a configuration that can maintain near-continuous PPC fire at extreme ranges, making the F configuration a dedicated sniper that excels in open terrain where its range advantage can be fully exploited. The lack of backup weapons or ammunition dependency makes it self-sufficient for extended operations, though it struggles in close-quarters environments.

Alternate Configuration T reworks the Prime's long-range focus into a devastating direct fire brawler. Twin ultra AC/10 autocannons, one per arm, deliver punishing burst damage at medium ranges, supplemented by an improved heavy medium laser in each arm for additional close-in firepower. A targeting computer enhances accuracy across all weapons, while a supercharger allows brief bursts of speed to help the normally ponderous Hel close to optimal engagement range. An SRM-4 in the right torso provides finishing capability against damaged opponents. The T configuration demands aggressive piloting to bring its medium-range weapons to bear, but rewards bold MechWarriors with overwhelming direct firepower.

text.deployment: Designed in 3136 by the Republic Institute of Strategic Combat, this variant is an experimental prototype built on the Blakist HEL-6X chassis, retaining its enhanced speed and triple strength myomer. Its most distinctive feature is a Chameleon Light Polarization Shield that gives it the outward appearance of a standard Capellan-produced Helios, enabling covert infiltration of enemy formations. The design carries an experimental RISC decoy viral jammer, an electronic warfare system that disrupts nearby electronic warfare interfaces, earning it the nickname "Squealios" for the audio distortion it produces. A remote drone command console and C3 slave unit support its role as a linchpin for black-ops ambush and raiding teams. Offensively, it mounts Clan-specification ER medium lasers, Clan SRM-6 launchers, and a plasma rifle. Reports indicate these units operated alongside EMP-6X Emperor variants during cross-Wall insertions onto Capellan-held worlds in the late 3130s and 3140s. One unit was pressed into service during the defense of London on Terra, though the fate of all surviving RISC Helios units following the fall of the Republic remains uncertain.

Introduced around 3144, this variant stands as a significant modernization of the Helios platform. Produced at the Ceres Metals facility on St. Ives with a new internal structure and gyro, this variant retains the proven Gauss rifle as its primary weapon while replacing the secondary armament with a pair of light PPCs and a multi-missile launcher. A C3 boosted slave unit provides enhanced networking capability compared to the earlier C3 variants. The 7L is seen almost exclusively operating alongside Vandal OmniMechs, suggesting it fills a dedicated role within specific Capellan combined-arms formations designed for coordinated long-range engagements.

text.overview: The Hercules was introduced in 3054 by Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corporation and Kali Yama Weapons Industries in response to a Free Worlds League request for a heavy BattleMech combining balanced mobility with substantial firepower. Designed from the outset as a versatile trooper capable of filling multiple combat roles, the seventy-ton Hercules mounts a diverse weapons array covering engagement ranges from extreme distance to point-blank. Powered by a Magna 350 XL engine that propels the chassis to speeds unusual for its weight class, the design fills the gap between slower assault platforms and lighter, less well-armed heavy designs. Production at facilities on Kendall and Kalidasa ensured steady supply to Free Worlds League Military formations, and the chassis quickly earned a reputation as a reliable all-around performer suited to missions ranging from air defense to direct fire support.
text.capabilities:
The Hercules is primarily intended as a mobile firing platform. Its Magna 350 XL fusion engine drives the seventy-ton chassis to a cruising speed of fifty-four kilometers per hour, with a flank speed of eighty-six, making it one of the faster designs in its weight class. This speed comes at the cost of jump capability, leaving the Hercules reliant on open terrain or careful route planning to avoid being outmaneuvered by lighter opponents. Eleven tons of Aldis Heavy ferro-fibrous armor provide protection sufficient to weather volleys from Clan OmniMechs and Inner Sphere opponents alike, giving MechWarriors confidence in sustained engagements.

The weapons loadout emphasizes versatility across all ranges. A Fusigon Model XI extended-range PPC serves as the primary weapon, capable of reaching targets at extreme distance. An Imperator Code Red LB 10-X autocannon supplements this at intermediate ranges, with the ability to switch between standard slugs and cluster munitions for anti-aircraft or anti-infantry work. Close-range defense falls to a Holly Streak SRM-2 launcher, an Aberdovey medium pulse laser, and two rear-mounted Martell small pulse lasers, the latter added specifically to counter Elemental swarming attacks. A Burow anti-missile system in the center torso provides additional protection against incoming missile fire. The design's primary weakness is a known electrical overload when struck by PPC fire, a flaw that has persisted despite the addition of damper circuits.
text.deployment: Introduced during the Dark Age, this variant is a significant modernization of the Hercules platform. The variant employs a composite internal structure to free tonnage for an Ultra-class autocannon, replacing the original LB 10-X and providing substantially increased ballistic firepower. Several of the original smaller weapons were removed to accommodate CASE II ammunition protection and an Angel ECM Suite, the latter providing electronic warfare capability absent from earlier models. This combination of enhanced firepower and electronic protection reflects the evolving battlefield of the post-Jihad era.
text.battleHistory:
The Hercules emerged from House Marik's desire for a new generation of heavy BattleMechs that could match the technological resurgence sweeping the Inner Sphere during the mid-thirty-first century. Kali Yama/Alphard Trading Corporation on Kendall and Kali Yama Weapons Industries on Kalidasa both commenced production in 3054, with the design entering Free Worlds League Military service shortly thereafter. The dual production lines ensured a steady supply of frames, and the Hercules quickly became a common sight in FWLM heavy and assault lances.

The Outworlds Alliance proved an unexpectedly significant customer, purchasing two dozen Hercules chassis, making the Periphery state the third-largest buyer after the FWLM and various mercenary commands. Given the higher cost of the Hercules compared to the older-technology designs typically sold to Periphery governments, the purchases attracted scrutiny. Suggestions that the Alliance intended to reverse-engineer the advanced technology proved unfounded, though especially only nineteen of the twenty-four units shipped were accounted for.

Operation Bulldog provided the Hercules its first major combat test against Clan forces, where it proved its worth against the Smoke Jaguars. The combination of long-range energy and ballistic weapons with close-range missile and laser systems proved devastating in the varied engagements of the campaign. Earlier, during Operation Guerrero, the design had performed satisfactorily but without particular distinction. It was in engagements against Clan opponents that the Hercules truly demonstrated its design philosophy, the mixed weapons array allowed MechWarriors to engage at whatever range the tactical situation demanded.

The Hercules also found success in the Solaris VII arenas, where representatives from Kali Yama Weapons Industries persuaded several stables and cooperatives to adopt the design. The chassis fared well in arena competition, further boosting its reputation and commercial appeal. During the Jihad, the Kalidasa facility fell under Word of Blake control while the Kendall plant continued production under Free Worlds League authority. Post-Jihad, the Kendall facility briefly operated under independent management before the reconstituted Free Worlds League reasserted control, introducing upgraded variants including the -9003 and -9004 models during the Dark Age era.

text.overview:
The Hermes II was introduced in 2798 by Irian BattleMechs Unlimited as a heavier successor to the original Star League-era Hermes. Designed as a heavy scout for the Free Worlds League Military, the forty-ton 'Mech combined respectable firepower with superior armor protection and reliable communications capabilities, filling a critical reconnaissance role in the post-Star League era. Early prototypes suffered from a flawed autocannon placement spread across the center torso, prompting a temporary laser-armed replacement while engineers consolidated the weapon into its final mounting.

The design earned the nickname "Old Reliable" for its exceptional ease of field maintenance, making it one of the most serviceable medium 'Mechs of its time. Production continued throughout the Succession Wars and beyond, with the Hermes II becoming a signature design of House Marik's military forces. The distinctive wing-like protrusions on the 'Mech's ankles, often mistaken for heat sinks, are purely cosmetic elements linking the design to its Hermes predecessor.
text.capabilities:
The Hermes II excels in restrictive terrain such as cities and forests, where its combination of speed, armor, and firepower gives it decisive advantages over lighter scouts. The Oriente autocannon provides reliable long-range firepower, while the Irian Weapons Works medium laser handles anti-'Mech duties at closer ranges. The Olympian flamer serves both anti-infantry purposes and enables the 'Mech's signature escape tactic, igniting surrounding terrain to blind enemy thermal sensors and discourage pursuit through the resulting inferno.

Seven and a half tons of Riese armor provides protection superior to most light 'Mechs the Hermes II is likely to encounter, allowing pilots to trade fire with enemy scouts or survive initial contact with heavier opponents long enough to withdraw. The Hermes 240 engine delivers a top speed of 97 kilometers per hour, sufficient to stay ahead of most pursuit.

The heart of the design is its Irian E.A.R. communications system, capable of direct satellite uplinks and tight-beam data bursts. This advanced system requires considerable surface area on the chassis, but grants reconnaissance teams exceptional coordination capabilities that have made the Hermes II invaluable for intelligence-gathering operations throughout its service history.
text.deployment: An advanced-technology refit developed in the late twenty-eighth century, this variant replaced the autocannon with extended-range large lasers in each side torso, supported by double heat sinks to manage the increased thermal load. This sophisticated configuration disappeared during the technological decline of the thirtieth century, with the design's heat sink technology becoming irreplaceable. Irian Technologies resumed limited production runs in the mid-3050s, building new units for Free Worlds League forces while also exporting the design back to the Draconis Combine where the original variant had once seen service.
text.battleHistory:
The Hermes II emerged from Irian BattleMechs Unlimited's massive production capacity during the military buildup following Kerensky's Exodus. Based on Star League-era Hermes schematics, the heavier design addressed the need for a more survivable scout platform. Production remained almost exclusively within the Free Worlds League throughout the Succession Wars, with only battlefield salvage and occasional mercenary sales bringing the design to other realms.

The Dark Shadows scout battalion, founded by Captain Janos DeVille in 3006, became closely associated with the Hermes II and its Mercury variant. Operating under SAFE's intelligence directorate, Dark Shadows units pioneered many of the reconnaissance tactics that defined the chassis's doctrine. DeVille later relinquished command to Captain Margarita Luhenson before rejoining the Fusiliers of Oriente, where he served during Duke Anton's revolt.

The Concord of Kapteyn opened new markets for the Hermes II, with the Draconis Combine purchasing chassis that Kuritan engineers would transform into the laser-armed Hermes III configuration. This variant proved popular enough to cement the design's reputation within the DCMS reconnaissance forces, eventually spawning a separate lineage of Luthien Armor Works upgrades.

Following the Clan Invasion and the Outreach Accords, Irian leveraged recovered lostech to produce the upgraded HER-5S, featuring an endo-steel chassis and ultra-class autocannon. Elite formations like the Free Worlds Guards received priority deliveries during the FWLM's massive upgrade program, with older models cascading down through the order of battle. This widespread distribution unfortunately meant substantial numbers fell into Word of Blake hands during their subversion of Free Worlds forces, with the Hermes II seeing service on both sides of the Jihad.

Post-Jihad recovery efforts led to continued evolution, while the ilClan era brought hybrid designs incorporating Clan technology acquired through various channels. Production continues at Irian and Shiro III facilities, ensuring the Hermes II remains a fixture of Free Worlds League reconnaissance doctrine centuries after its introduction.

production.communications: Irian E.A.R. Special Mk. II with Guardian ECM and C3 Slave

text.deployment: This variant represents Luthien Armor Works' comprehensive modernization of salvaged Hermes III frames recovered following the Jihad. Twin Lord's Light 5 snub-nose PPCs replace the original large lasers, providing effective medium-range firepower with improved damage potential at the cost of maximum engagement distance. The addition of a second hand actuator (replacing the original flamer) improves the 'Mech's utility during extended reconnaissance operations where object manipulation may prove necessary. Advanced electronics including Guardian ECM, C3 slave integration, and an upgraded targeting computer transform the aging scout into a capable network-enabled reconnaissance platform.

production.communications: Unknown with Angel ECM and Bloodhound Probe

text.deployment: Luthien Armor Works' newest Hermes III variant addresses longstanding criticisms of the design's speed relative to dedicated light scouts. A supercharger provides burst acceleration capability, while a Bloodhound probe and Angel ECM offer formidable electronic warfare capabilities superior to the standard Guardian suite. Twin Clan-specification ER large lasers (reportedly acquired from dwindling Nova Cat stocks) provide extended-range firepower that restores the engagement envelope the snub-nose PPCs of the 6K variant sacrificed. LAW hopes this configuration will prove the definitive version of the Hermes III chassis.

text.overview:
The Highlander is one of the most iconic assault BattleMechs in the history of the Inner Sphere, first entering service with the Star League Defense Force in 2592. Designed by StarCorps Industries as a dedicated city and installation defender, the ninety-ton design combined a versatile weapons mix, heavy ferro-fibrous armor protection, and an unusual feature for an assault chassis: jump jets that granted it tactical mobility unmatched by its peers. This agility proved so effective that within decades of its introduction, nearly every Regular and Royal Army BattleMech regiment featured Highlanders in their ranks.

Perhaps more than any other single design, the Highlander is defined by the infamous "Highlander Burial", a death-from-above attack in which the 'Mech leaps onto a lighter opponent and literally drives it into the ground. So popular was this devastating tactic that StarCorps reengineered the Highlander's legs specifically to withstand repeated such attacks, transforming a desperation move into a signature combat technique feared across every battlefield in the Inner Sphere and beyond.
text.capabilities:
The Highlander carries a weapons mix optimized for ranged engagements that remains effective when ranges close. The primary weapon of the original HGN-732 is an M-7 Gauss rifle capable of delivering devastating kinetic impacts at extreme range, backed by a Holly LRM-20 launcher for sustained long-range fire support. At closer distances, a Holly SRM-6 rack and a pair of Harmon Starclass medium lasers provide significant short-range firepower. Two tons of ammunition for each launcher system and the Gauss rifle provide excellent battlefield endurance, while CASE protects the MechWarrior from catastrophic ammunition explosions.

Fifteen and a half tons of Grumman-3 ferro-fibrous armor make the Highlander exceptionally well protected for its class, while three HildCo Model 10 jump jets grant it a mobility advantage that most assault 'Mechs cannot match. This combination of firepower, protection, and mobility allows the Highlander to control engagement ranges, pursue fleeing opponents, and execute the feared Highlander Burial with devastating effect. The design's relatively low heat output allows pilots to maintain a near-continuous barrage, though sustained use of all weapons systems simultaneously still demands thermal discipline.
text.deployment: This custom configuration replaces the standard 732's weapons suite with an ER PPC, a prototype Streak SRM-6, twin Medium Pulse Lasers, and a pair of LRM-15 missile launchers. Fourteen double heat sinks manage the substantially increased thermal output. The modification serves as a significant departure from the original Highlander weapons philosophy, trading the Gauss rifle's long-range precision for the ER PPC's sustained energy output while maintaining robust missile capability at all ranges.
text.battleHistory:
Designed for the Star League Defense Force in 2592, the Highlander was an instant success with both Regular and Royal regiments. Its wide variety of weapons and jump jets allowed it to take on any situation, and the design rapidly became one of the most common assault 'Mechs in the SLDF order of battle. The Highlander saw extensive service through the final decades of the Star League era, and many accompanied General Aleksandr Kerensky on the Exodus, where Clan scientists would eventually upgrade surviving chassis into the formidable Highlander IIC using advanced Clan technology.

The Succession Wars devastated Highlander production in the Inner Sphere. StarCorps' factory on Son Hoa was destroyed toward the end of the Second Succession War, driving the original HGN-732 to virtual extinction. An agreement between Hollis Incorporated and StarCorps to rebuild destroyed chassis from scratch using readily available technology produced the downgraded HGN-733, which Hollis continued to custom-build on Corey until the Fourth Succession War when the licensing arrangement was revoked. By the mid-3030s, StarCorps had managed to restart limited production on Son Hoa, producing barely a dozen new 'Mechs per year.

Throughout the Succession Wars, ComStar secretly maintained a large stock of original Highlanders inherited from the Star League. During the War of 3039, ComStar provided both HGN-733s and a few advanced HGN-732s to the Draconis Combine, shocking Lyran forces who encountered what they believed to be extinct Star League-era technology. The Northwind Highlanders also maintained a disproportionate number of operational Highlanders through the Succession Wars, many with original Star League-era components, and their skill with the Highlander Burial became legendary.

By 3057, StarCorps' Son Hoa factory had returned to full production, producing original-specification HGN-732 Highlanders for Lyran units of the Federated Commonwealth. The FedCom Civil War spurred the development of multiple advanced variants, including the urban-combat focused HGN-734 and the ComStar-enhanced HGN-736. The HGN-734's debut in 3062 also had an unexpected civilian legacy: the production changeover left a surplus of older-specification components, which StarCorps repurposed to create the St. Florian FireMech, one of the most advanced IndustrialMechs introduced since the fall of the Star League. Post-Civil War production continued to diversify, with the HGN-738 introducing Heavy Gauss Rifle technology and the experimental HGN-641-X-2 pushing the boundaries of what the venerable chassis could accommodate.

The Word of Blake Jihad severely disrupted Highlander production when Blakist forces attacked the Son Hoa factories in 3074, rendering them temporarily inoperable. Meanwhile, Clan Wolf had established its own Highlander legacy on Weingarten, converting salvaged Inner Sphere chassis into Highlander IICs at the W-7 Facilities, an operation that would eventually pass to Clan Hell's Horses when they captured the planet in 3142. Production of new Inner Sphere variants eventually resumed on Son Hoa, and designs such as the HGN-740 continued to emerge well into the Dark Age. The Highlander's long and distinguished service record, combined with its association with the famed Northwind Highlanders mercenary brigade, has cemented its place as one of the most recognized and respected assault 'Mechs in the history of mechanized warfare.
